appearance.bark_look.thickness.note: The genus's bark thickness as its reference species', alnus-rubra (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/alnus-rubra.json): text: FOFEM 0.026; 'rarely more than 1/4 inch' (Sargent), <1.9 cm (FEIS)

appearance.bark_look.stages.grey.note: The genus's grey stage as its reference species, alnus-rubra, shows it (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/alnus-rubra.json): stage: text: 'gray, smooth ... lenticels inconspicuous' (FNA); 'roughened by minute wart-like excrescences, pale gray or nearly white' (Sargent); mottled (FEIS). White lichen is habitat, not bark; until_diameter_m: inferred (photo)

appearance.bark_look.stages.plated base.note: The genus's plated base stage as its reference species, alnus-rubra, shows it (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/alnus-rubra.json): stage: text: 'darkening and breaking into shallow rectangular plates in age' (FNA)

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 genus aggregate for Alnus (gwddagg_v2.2_genus.csv, read): specific gravity 0.47 (wsg_est, the hierarchical-model genus mean, from 567 records in 40 sources); trunks 0.47, branches 0.47. A species with its own measurements states its own. Basic density is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: FNA's account of the genus: the leaves are three-ranked to nearly two-ranked, so one stands at each node.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: FNA's account of the genus: the leaves, on long or short shoots, are three-ranked to nearly two-ranked.

traits.flowering_position.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual's Alnus chapter (read in full): male and female catkins ripen on the previous year's twigs; FEIS's red alder review (page read) puts the staminate catkins in clusters near a twig's end, beside its shoot, not ending it.
